title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 39
paragraphs: Eight days had now passed while they sat opposite one another, when Timagenides gave this advice to Mardonius. Mardonius, seeing that the advice was good, sent the cavalry, when night came on, to the pass of Kithairon leading toward Plataea — which the Boeotians call “Three Heads” and the Athenians “Oak Heads.” Sent in this way, the cavalry did not act in vain: they caught five hundred pack-animals coming out into the plain, carrying provisions from the Peloponnese to the army, along with the men accompanying the carts. Having taken this prize, the Persians began slaughtering them without sparing either beast or man; and when they were sated with killing, they surrounded what was left and drove them into the camp to Mardonius.
